But I can't really dedicate myself to figuring out how to write this draft into this format without the green lights for the concept first. That's what the Drafts and Critiques forum is for, right?

Uhhh sort of but not really; the drafts critique forum is for giving feedback on this as a draft and assumes you have attempted to answer the question of 'how do you get this into the format' already. Whereas I want to know you've at least considered it because guess what buddy: the format imposes restrictions on how you can tell the story; and if you don't consider how those restrictions are gonna impact the story telling, you're gonna have a bad day when you try to write this.

As for the actual longer form exploration, I'm kinda…torn on it. If executed well, this could be really good, and I can totally see this working well; but it feels like is has a lot of potential to be really dry and boring, and I think what'll really elevate this is the characterisation: making everyone really feel real, and showing enough of the monster that it feels like a viable threat; and like…really having us understand why what's happening is interesting.

I'm still really not convinced by this as a goi-format: it really feels like a lot of this detail would be best kept as a tale; since like, it feels like a lot of times this would be quiet informal stuff you don't necessarily want to admit to doing in an official report (e.g., the two indian soldiers being ordered to shoot the chinese ones if they return alone).

I will greenlight this under the assumption you deeply think about how you tell this story and really consider what the best format for it is.

item.title: Re: GOC Threat Entity Entry (India/China)
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

I'll be honest with you, I'm still trying to get my head around the GOC format. But I can't really dedicate myself to figuring out how to write this draft into this format without the green lights for the concept first. That's what the Drafts and Critiques forum is for, right? I'll either figure this out by myself or get some help. So really, translating my concept into a GOC format hopefully wouldn't be too much of a concern. Unless, you actually want me to figure this out first?

So anyways, to address your concern, I can only put so much into a pitch before some admin here tell me to simplify it or trim the fat. Believe me, I would love to give you more detail for the initial pitch. However, since we're in the discussion section, I can tell you in more detail.

So, how this will play out is that both India and China want to send in their agents in to take care of the threat entities plaguing the border disputed area. And yes, this is to the dismay of other occult members. After all, their mission statement is;

"To keep the peace and maintain friendly relations between occult organizations, protect humanity against all threats paranormal, parascientific, and paratemporal, and take any actions required to ensure the survival of the human race."

But here's the thing. We both know that's not how the world works. Unfortunately, politics, national interests and basic human stubbornness prevents that cooperation from happening. It's like this, if it were in the best interest of humanity to stop global warming, why haven't all the world leaders done so already? And I do mean all of them. So yeah, same logic here. Just because it's a danger to humanity, doesn't mean humanity would ever stop playing politics.

Now, as for why GOC wouldn't just reject both China and India then send their own agents in to kill the monster. You must understand something here. Both China and India have a large landmass. That landmass contains a, and pardon my language here, metric FUCK ton of undocumented threat entities that's just left unchecked. For either of them to quit the GOC and form their own organization would be detrimental for the mission of the GOC. If both China and India would no longer cooperate with the GOC and even actively arrest or kill GOC operatives on their soil, that would mean a good chunk of the world is just simply unprotected. Or worse, they may even leak out information about these threat entities to the wider public. I don't even think GOC could or even would retaliate. To do so would be an act of war and who knows how many would die just by fighting in it. In other words, the GOC has to not appear antagonistic to either countries if they wish to have easy access to their landmass.

So how the GOC would resolve this issue is by appointing a team consisting of seven Indian agents, five chinese agents and one Chinese-American Indian as their leader. Yes, this does make China a bit low key pissed off, but they went with it because they can at the very least still claim it’s a “Chinese-lead” mission.

Anyways, here’s the overview of the story. Feel free to give feedback.

The team tracked this family of rock monsters into a cave. The team went into the cave trying to kill the monsters. But as they ventured in, a Chinese agent went missing. As they went deeper, another Chinese agent went missing. Then another. There are now two mainland Chinese agents in the cave now. As we all know, we humans are emotional creatures, even the most hardened veterans still have emotions to some degree and one of these emotions is paranoia. At this moment, they should feel outnumbered and targeted. So the Chinese agents are certainly feeling the tension now. They then found themselves in a branching path. There are two tunnels leading somewhere. So the leader splits the team up into two. The two Chinese agents are sticking with the leader because the Chinese-American Indian is still Chinese in blood, so like it or not, they feel as if they can trust him. He then assigns one of the seven Indians to be the leader of team two, takes two Indians with him and goes in their separate tunnels. Now what we have now is a team consisting of the leader, two Chinese and two Indians, the other consists of all five Indians.

Team 1 goes into the tunnel. As they get farther in, an Indian dies. But unlike with the other three which disappeared, this one has a corpse. The body does have bullet holes in it and there was gunshot residue on the weapon of the Indian that died and the two Chinese. What is known in that situation is that they first heard a scream, then gunshots and then the Indian is dead. Was this an accident brought on by panic? Was this murder? Was this the work of the monster? The situation right now is tense and the last Indian of the group is panicking a bit. The Chinese swore they saw the monster attacking the Indian and they simply open fired. The Indian claims he saw the two Chinese pointed their weapons at him and fired, but he’s not sure if that’s what happened. The Indian tried to message the other team about this potential betrayal, but was overheard by the leader. Leader tries to calm him down and tries to keep the group together. He decides they should all go back and regroup. But as they went back, the last Indian wants to at least get the corpse of the Indian back outside so it can be properly cremated and have his ashes placed next to his other fallen brothers. This was rebuffed by the two Chinese stating that the monster could get them at any moment and carrying a corpse would slow them down. But since the leader was a bit more sympathetic, he ordered one of the Chinese to help carry the body by the foot. Once they got to the intersection where the two tunnels meet into one, the Chinese helped carrying the body stopped and told the Indian still carrying the body that he should get one of his own to help carry the corpse. He left him there and went to the group and told the other Indians that he helped and now someone else will switch with him. Naturally the Indians got a mod at him for disrespecting their fallen, but decided to just begrudgingly thank the Chinese and went to help the Indian carrying the corpse. But when they looked back, the Indian and the corpse disappeared. You can understand how pissed off the Indians were at this.

They eventually got out of the cave and tried to rethink their strategy and as well as try to cool off. However, the Indian that was incharge of team 2 wanted the leader to step down since under his lead, two of the Indians were killed off. Most of the Indians supported this because under his leadership, team 2 never lost a member. They argued for a bit and eventually agreed to have two agents stationed outside in the entrance of the cave while the rest went back in. The leader obviously wants everyone to go back in and not split up this time. But to prevent a mutiny, this compromise was reached. Secretly, the two Indians were told to shoot on sight if the only people came out were Chinese. Officially, the entire team went in, but in reality, two teams were. Team one with the leader and the two Chinese and team two with the Indian leader and two Indians. So how this will end is that the leader will try to reason with the Indian leader and maybe lower the tension. Then one of the Indian agents got pissed off because he doesn’t trust the Chinese and doesn’t want the rest of the Indians to trust them either. Reason left him for a moment as the leader and the Indian leader actually agreed to set their feelings aside, stormed off. The leader asked the nearest agents to go get him, which were the Chinese. Then there was a scream and gunshots. The group quickly went over and saw only the two Chinese remain. Panicked, the Indian leader pointed his weapon at the two Chinese and demanded to know what they did with the Indian. The Chinese swore they did nothing to the Indians. The leader tried to calm everyone down, only for the Indian leader to then point the weapon at him. Seeing this, the two Chinese pointed their weapon at the Indian leader and demanded that he lower his weapon. Seeing this, the other Indian pointed his weapon at the Chinese. This situation just got more intense as a Mexican standoff just happened. One wrong move or word would mean everyone dies. But suddenly, all this noise has attracted the monster. And then

[*LOG REDACTED FOR EXTRANEOUS DATA*]

Target liquidated.

One indian walks out.

So how’s that? Would this be okay?

Page Type: Other (GOC Entry)

To be real clear here: you mean you're wanting to write a GOC goi-format in the style of e.g. KTE-5634-Ex-Machina-Bosch?

My, big concern with this pitch is that I have a good idea of you wanting to like, get into the conflict between the GOC members as an analogue for like border disputes, and to really explore how this infighting affects them; but my concern is that you've spent a lot of time talking in the generic and I don't really know if you've nailed down the specific: that is, how this conflict between members is actually intended to play out. Like, how does it escalate? How does it end up getting resolved? What does happen when a team composed of these two nations that hate each other are sent on a mission in the background of their heated political dispute?

I have some concerns about this as a GoI Format: it feels to me that a tale would allow you to write this conflict a lot more effectively, with less of a worry about how you include this lengthy conflict in a way that feels like…appropriately cold and clinical? Like, the threat entity database entry idea is great when the GOC are unified and when you can tell a story in a very detached and cold way; but it feels to me that this wants to really get into the story and really intimately play with the characters?

⤱Critique V2⤱
Cheese of different nations

So at the end, you mentioned how the team members slowly disappears, and grow more and more suspicious of each other, till finally the captain is the lone survivor. This feels like a very cheap ending, and the overall message of your story changes radically. It's now less about trying to reconcile the differences between people of differing views, and more like hey, people are destined to never be able to see eye to eye. Which admittedly, is less of a sell for me.

Also, this sudden disappearance of the team members, from either the other team members, or the monsters, just… doesn't add up. You mentioned how they suspect that their own team members may have been secretly tasked to kill them, but makes the story so much more convoluted, and frankly doesn't make sense. Isn't killing them going to create more problems for both sides? No one benefits in any way. And, these are GOC soldiers. Who normally go for psych screenings, have been put in similar situations. You could say that they're better than the average human being, both in terms of physical and mental capability. I could imagine a heated arguement turned into a struggle, but murder is pretty far off.

And to echo what Cyvstvi said earlier, the monsters are a minor aspect of the story. In this story, it's technically the primary objective, but as it progresses, you can see that it becomes a secondary objective, compared to the resolution of the dispute between the teammates.



Conclusion: There's a lot of things going on now, that the story becomes very complicated and convoluted. You need to realign your focus on what matters, which is the team.

Additionally, I would suggest you go online and learn about how to handle/facilitate discussions, and how to create win-win situations out of problems, so as to give your article a more solid feel and credibility.

Once you have made the adjustments, or you have any questions, feel free to reach out to me on Wikidot PM or on IRC chat.

item.title: Re: GOC Threat Entity Entry (India/China)
item.content:encoded:
⤱Critique⤱
Nationalist Cheese

So first off, it feels weird that the GOC would send a team comprising of agents from the country involved in the conflict? I could think of some reasons such as familiarity with the surroundings, easier to blend in, quickest team to respond< but I want to know what's your reason.

Now, I'm an Indian person (albeit not living in India) and so there's always been this rivalry between our two countries, not just from this issue. So I'm curious to see how you handle the tension between members of the two nationalities. Keep in mind however, to avoid any sort of bias in your storytelling. Remember, this is an ongoing political incident.

Besides that, the same will be said about the entire political incident. While you may have your opinions about who is write or wrong, DO NOT integrate them into your story. Make it as a neutral as it can be, so that you don't offend anyone. This is meant to be an article that can be read and understood by everyone.

Also, just a minor detail, is the team being sent in Assessment or STRIKE? These teams have 2 different purposes as well as operating procedures, so make your choices and integrate it into the story.



Conclusion: Overall, you have an interesting storyline here, that is worth pursuing. However, do be careful of how you portray the conflict, since it is a sensitive issue.

Once you have made the adjustments, or you have any questions, feel free to reach out to me on Wikidot PM or on IRC chat.
